c.tagline: Basque reinvention — Guggenheim titanium, old-town pintxos, green hills.

taxi.fareNote: Metered; Uber presence is limited, so licensed street/rank taxis and the Cabify and Bolt apps are the norm. An airport supplement applies.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Casco Viejo and on transit

hood_desc: Bilbao's medieval old town — the Siete Calles (Seven Streets), Santiago Cathedral, arcaded Plaza Nueva and the covered Ribera Market. A walkable maze of pintxos bars and shops, lively day and night; best for first-timers who want atmosphere and the classic txikiteo bar-hop.

The elegant 19th-century modern centre on the west bank, home to the Guggenheim Museum, the Zubizuri footbridge, grand Gran Via shopping and Abando station. Wide avenues, upscale hotels and easy transport make it a calm, convenient first-time base, especially for families.

A busy commercial district beside Abando around Plaza Indautxu and the Azkuna Zentroa (Alhondiga) cultural centre, with the Fine Arts Museum and Dona Casilda park nearby. Packed with shops, restaurants and the lively 'Pozas' bar street — good for shopping and going out.

The gritty-turned-hip quarter across the river from Casco Viejo — Bilbao's bohemian, multicultural core of street art, galleries, vintage shops and buzzing bars. San Frantzisko is also the city's LGBT hub. Best for younger travellers after an alternative, going-out scene.

A student neighbourhood across the Nervion around the University of Deusto, with riverside promenades, green space and everyday local prices. Well connected by metro yet away from the tourist crush — a relaxed, budget-friendly base.

water.note: Tap water is safe and good quality.

transit.hours: The metro runs about 6am-11pm on weekdays, until 2am on Fridays and all night on Saturdays; night Gautxori buses cover the small hours on other nights.
transit.pay: Get a rechargeable Barik card (about EUR 3) from metro machines and top it up; a single Barik metro ride is roughly EUR 0.90-1.80 by zone, versus EUR 1.80-2.60 for a paper single. The same Barik card works on Metro Bilbao, the Euskotren tram, Bilbobus, Bizkaibus and the Artxanda funicular, and contactless bank-card tap-in is rolling out.

ferry: Port of Bilbao (Brittany Ferries to Portsmouth, UK)

transit.m: Bizkaibus A3247 to Bilbao centre/Termibus (~25 min, every 15-20 min)

tip.r: Round up or leave 5-10% for good service; not obligatory.

food.name: Pintxos crawl
food.desc: Bar-top snacks eaten one bar at a time: gilda skewers of anchovy, olive and guindilla, txistorra, tortilla wedges and croquetas.

places.name: Cafe Bar Bilbao
places.note: Handsome tiled bar on the arcaded square, one of the best-loved all-round pintxo stops.

places.name: Gure Toki
places.note: Award-winning modern pintxos alongside classics; consistently on best-of lists.

places.name: Victor Montes
places.note: Long-standing Basque bar-restaurant with a marble counter piled with traditional pintxos.

food.name: Bacalao al pil-pil
food.desc: Salt cod cooked gently in olive oil and garlic until the fish gelatin emulsifies into a silky yellow sauce. The Basque test of a kitchen.

places.name: Cafe Bar Bilbao
places.note: Known for its bacalao al pil-pil pintxo, a good low-commitment way to try the dish.

places.name: Victor Montes
places.note: Serves the full plated version plus pil-pil pintxos in a former market space.

places.name: Restaurante Rio-Oja
places.note: No-frills Old Town institution serving cazuelas of cod, tripe and squid in ink.

food.name: Marmitako
food.desc: Fisherman's stew of fresh bonito tuna, potato, onion and choricero pepper, simmered until the broth turns paprika-orange and thick.

places.name: Restaurante Rio-Oja
places.note: Old-school clay-pot cooking; the place locals send you for stews rather than pintxos.

places.name: Berton
places.note: Quality-obsessed Old Town bar and dining room with traditional Basque dishes and good wine.

places.name: Mercado de la Ribera food hall
places.note: Riverside market with counters cooking Basque stews and seafood from the stalls below.

food.name: Bacalao a la vizcaina
food.desc: Salt cod in a deep red sauce built from dried choricero peppers and slow-cooked onion. Sweeter and earthier than pil-pil.

places.name: Restaurante Rio-Oja
places.note: Classic Biscay cod done in cazuela at fair prices, part of the standing Old Town menu.

places.name: Victor Montes
places.note: Traditional Basque restaurant upstairs from the pintxo counter for full plates.

places.name: Berton Sasibil
places.note: Sit-down sibling of Berton with cod dishes and Basque classics on the daily menu.

food.name: Txuleta de buey
food.desc: Thick, dry-aged rib chop from old dairy cattle, seared over embers, salted heavily and served rare in slices. Shared between two.

places.name: Casa Rufo
places.note: Tiny grocer-turned-restaurant behind shelves of wine, famed among locals for its txuleton.

places.name: Asador Getaria
places.note: Coal-grill asador doing whole turbot and txuleta in a wood-panelled dining room.

places.name: Mercado de la Ribera food hall
places.note: Grill counters serve smaller steak portions if you are not up for a whole chop.

food.name: Carolina and pastel de arroz
food.desc: Bilbao pastry-shop sweets: the meringue-topped Carolina tart and a small, custardy rice cake eaten mid-morning with coffee.

places.name: Pasteleria Arrese
places.note: Century-old Bilbao pastry house and one of the classic addresses for Carolinas.

places.name: Martina de Zuricalday
places.note: Bilbao confectioner dating to the 1830s, still turning out the city's traditional cakes.

places.name: Pasteleria Don Manuel
places.note: Old Town bakery counter for pastel de arroz and other Basque morning pastries.

food.name: Txakoli
food.desc: Bone-dry, faintly fizzy Basque white poured from a height to aerate it. Low in alcohol and made for seafood pintxos.

places.name: Berton
places.note: Serious wine list with Bizkaiko Txakolina poured by the glass and the theatrical pour.

places.name: Gure Toki
places.note: Txakoli alongside its prize-winning pintxos on the Old Town's main square.

places.name: Mercado de la Ribera food hall
places.note: Several bars pour local txakoli by the glass beside the river.

food.name: Kalimotxo
food.desc: Basque invention of red wine cut half-and-half with cola over ice. Cheap, refreshing and the fuel of every Bilbao street party.

places.name: Bar Irrintzi
places.note: Buzzy Old Town bar popular with a young crowd for kalimotxo and creative pintxos.

places.name: Bars around Plaza Nueva
places.note: Nearly every arcade bar pours it; join the crowd spilling into the square in the evening.

places.name: Bars along Calle Ledesma
places.note: After-work pintxo street where kalimotxo and small beers keep flowing late.

landmarks: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
Frank Gehry's titanium ship of swirling curves transformed a rusting port city into an art pilgrimage, guarded by Jeff Koons' flower-covered Puppy and Louise Bourgeois' spider.
Casco Viejo (Old Town)
The medieval Seven Streets pack pintxo bars, boutiques and buskers into a lively riverside maze centered on Santiago Cathedral and the arcaded Plaza Nueva.
Plaza Nueva
This elegant neoclassical arcaded square is Bilbao's pintxo epicenter, its colonnades sheltering celebrated taverns and a Sunday flea market of books and songbirds.
Mercado de la Ribera
Europe's largest covered market, an Art Deco riverboat of stained glass moored beside the estuary, brims with Basque produce and gastro-bar counters.
Vizcaya Bridge (Puente Colgante)
The world's oldest transporter bridge, a UNESCO-listed 1893 iron colossus at Portugalete, still ferries cars and passengers in a hanging gondola across the Nervión.
Funicular de Artxanda
A century-old funicular hoists visitors to Mount Artxanda's balcony viewpoint, where the whole sweep of Bilbao's valley and Gehry's titanium curves unfolds below.
Zubizuri Bridge
Santiago Calatrava's white steel footbridge arcs across the Nervión like a harp, linking riverside promenades on the walk between old town and Guggenheim.
Catedral de Santiago
Bilbao's Gothic cathedral, a stop on the coastal Camino de Santiago, hides a lovely cloister and porticoed Angel Gate within the Casco Viejo's lanes.
Museo de Bellas Artes
One of Spain's finest regional art museums pairs El Greco, Goya and Zurbarán with Basque masters, a classical counterweight to the Guggenheim nearby.
Azkuna Zentroa (Alhóndiga)
Philippe Starck reimagined a 1909 wine warehouse as a cultural center resting on 43 fantastical columns, complete with a glass-bottomed rooftop pool.

train.note: No direct international trains. Renfe long-distance services from Bilbao Abando reach Madrid in about 5 hours and Barcelona in 6h30, and the narrow-gauge Renfe Feve line runs a slow scenic route west along the Cantabrian coast to Santander and Oviedo. For France you travel to Irún/Hendaye and change onto SNCF. A high-speed link to Vitoria and the Basque Y is under construction.

bus.note: Everything leaves from Termibus at San Mamés, on the metro and tram. Coaches are often faster than the train in northern Spain - San Sebastián takes about an hour, Santander 1h20 and Madrid under 5 hours. Bring your passport for the French services, though the border crossing itself is a Schengen formality.

ferry.note: The UK and Ireland sailings leave from the outer port at Zierbena, about 20 km from the city centre rather than from Bilbao itself - allow time and check the shuttle arrangements. Crossings take a day or more across the Bay of Biscay, cabins are compulsory and the route is popular with drivers avoiding the long haul through France. Frequencies drop in winter.

half.name: San Sebastián
half.blurb: A Basque coastal city known for its curving Concha beach, Belle Époque architecture, and dense concentration of pintxos bars.

half.name: Gernika-Lumo
half.blurb: The Basque town bombed in 1937, an event immortalized in Picasso's Guernica, today home to the Basque Country's historic parliament oak.

half.name: San Juan de Gaztelugatxe
half.blurb: A small islet crowned by a hermitage, connected to the mainland by a stone bridge and 241 winding steps.

full.name: Santander
full.blurb: A port city on Spain's northern coast with a long sweep of urban beach and the modernist Botín art center on the bay.

full.name: Pamplona
full.blurb: A Navarrese city famous for the Running of the Bulls each July, with a walled old town and citadel park.
